I've been working with a local coffee roasting company, and they asked me to develop product label design for a special batch crafted blend that rotates monthly. The link is one of the original art proofs. The final ink colors were Pantone 871 Metallic Gold C, Dark Grey PMS Cool Gray 11 C, and Black. The labels were screen printed on White vinyl substrate. I doubt anyone here is familiar with the brand, but all of the elements in the design borrow from key elements from their previous corporate branding. Thanks for looking! Feedback and constructive criticism is always welcome.

Looks good. It has a very rustic, vintage feel to it. Two small constructive feedbacks though:

Would it be possible to tone down the white stripes in the centre? They seem to take over the hierarchy a little bit.

Secondly, is there enough space to create more space around the edges? The content goes within a mm of the edge of the sticker.. I'd try to get a consistent space around the border. This also helps if the printers guillotine is off by a mm or so. Does that make sense?

Edit: The capitalisation in inconsistent: "small batch * Exotic * distinctive". You may as well capatalist all the words: "Small batch * Exotic * Distinctive"

Thank you candid feedback! The white stripes are admittedly harsh, and perhaps too contrasting. They are made up of unprinted material and act as a 4th color. Budget was somewhat of an issue on these labels, and adding an additional imprint color unfortunately wasn't in the cards... You are SPOT ON, regarding the tight registration. The customer approved the attached layout design, but I was so Obsessive Compulsively afraid that the registration might be slightly off (at the time of cutting) that I did scale down all of the artwork to be farther into a "safe zone". The only areas that bleed off the edge are the black background, stripes, and gold horizontal bars. Thanks again for looking, and ESPECIALLY for taking the time to critique!
That's ok. Great work, and be sure to post more stuff for us to look at!
